assumptions: The lower and upper inequalities are the paper's interlacing chain d_1 < lambda_1 < d_2 < ... < d_n < lambda_n, written for zero-based finite indices.
p54SecularWeight is the squared modified coordinate in equation (3.2).
p54Characteristic and p54DeletedCharacteristic are the full and one-factor-deleted products in the displayed determinant identity preceding equation (3.2).

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p54_t3_inverse_secular_construction (n : Nat) (hn : 0 < n) (d lambda : P54Vector n) (hd : StrictMono d) (hlower : forall i, d i < lambda i) (hupper : forall i j, i < j -> lambda i < d j) : (forall i, 0 < p54SecularWeight d lambda i) and p54Characteristic lambda = p54Characteristic d + sum i, Polynomial.C (p54SecularWeight d lambda i) * p54DeletedCharacteristic d i
formal_statement.plain_language: Show that interlacing makes every squared modified coordinate positive and that the coordinates from (3.2) reproduce the proposed characteristic polynomial.

informal_proof: Interlacing gives the numerator and denominator in (3.2) the same sign. The two characteristic products have equal leading terms, so their difference has degree below n. At each node d_i, that difference equals the numerator in (3.2). Interpolating from the n distinct nodes and substituting the weights reconstructs the displayed characteristic-product identity.
informal_statement: Prove the positivity and inverse characteristic-product identity asserted around equations (3.2)-(3.3).
